objective_for_doctor: A 17-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: loss of consciousness.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve lost consciousness, and I’ve also been coughing up blood, with significant shortness of breath/difficulty breathing. I have sharp pain (intensity 4/10) in my chest areas (right/left side of the chest and posterior chest wall) and it radiates to my left/right scapula and posterior chest wall.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this sounds urgent; are you currently still short of breath, and did the loss of consciousness happen before or after the coughing up blood?  
Doctor: Do you have any history of blood clots, recent long travel/immobility, use of hormonal contraception, fever, or recent trauma to your chest?

Yes— I currently have significant shortness of breath/difficulty breathing. The loss of consciousness happened with these other symptoms, but I don’t know whether it was before or after I started coughing up blood.

Yes—I have had deep vein thrombosis (DVT). I’ve traveled out of the country to North America in the last 4 weeks, and I’ve been unable to move or get up for more than 3 consecutive days within the last 4 weeks. I currently take hormones. I don’t know about fever or recent trauma to my chest, but I did have surgery within the last month.

Doctor: I’m very concerned for a life-threatening pulmonary embolism (blood clot in the lung); I need to confirm urgently—can you tell me if you have had any fever, rapid heartbeat/palpitations, or leg swelling/pain in the past week?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CT Pulmonary Angiography (or V/Q scan if contrast contraindicated) + REQUEST TEST: D-dimer + REQUEST TEST: CBC/CMP + REQUEST TEST: ECG + REQUEST TEST: Chest X-ray.

I don’t know whether I’ve had fever or a rapid heartbeat/palpitations.  

Yes—I have swelling in the posterior aspect of my ankle (right).

Doctor: Given your DVT history, recent immobility and hormonal use, plus hemoptysis, chest pain, and new ankle swelling, I’m treating this as a massive pulmonary embolism until proven otherwise—are you able to tell me your current oxygen saturation if you have it, and do you feel faint/lightheaded right now?  
Doctor: I’m also ordering an immediate bedside exam: REQUEST TEST: Bedside oxygen saturation + REQUEST TEST: Repeat vitals (HR, BP, RR, O2 sat) + REQUEST TEST: Troponin/BNP (for right-heart strain) + REQUEST TEST: ABG if available.

I don’t know my oxygen saturation. I’ve lost consciousness, and I have significant shortness of breath/difficulty breathing right now, but I don’t know whether I feel faint/lightheaded at this moment.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as a massive pulmonary embolism causing shock—can you tell me if you’re getting worse while sitting still, and whether you can speak full sentences or only a few words?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Immediate bedside echocardiography (right ventricular strain) and REQUEST TEST: Coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT) + REQUEST TEST: Type & screen.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Massive pulmonary embolism (likely from DVT related to recent immobility and hormonal contraception), with hemoptysis and syncope.
